facts.statement: The holotype specimen RRBP 08630 was collected in 2008 at the Namba 2 locality.
facts.quote: RRBP 08630 was collected during 2008 at Namba 2 locality

facts.statement: All known specimens of Rukwasuchus were found approximately 25 km south of Lake Rukwa in southwestern Tanzania.
facts.quote: All specimens came from approximately 25 km south of Lake Rukwa in the Galula Study Area, Rukwa Rift Basin of southwestern Tanzania

facts.statement: Rukwasuchus was named by Joseph J. W. Sertich and Patrick M. O'Connor in 2014.
facts.quote: Rukwasuchus was named by Joseph J. W. Sertich and Patrick M. O'Connor in 2014

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis generally places Rukwasuchus within the clade Peirosauria.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analysis generally recover Rukwasuchus as being a member of the clade Peirosauria

facts.statement: Rukwasuchus is classified either within the family Peirosauridae or as a basal member of the family Itasuchidae.
facts.quote: either within Peirosauridae as originally proposed or more recently as a basal member of the family Itasuchidae

facts.statement: Some features of the brain of Rukwasuchus suggest it may have had more terrestrial habits, unlike some related forms interpreted as semi-aquatic.
facts.quote: While several purportedly closely related forms have been interpreted as semi-aquatic, some features of the brain of Rukwasuchus may indicate more terrestrial habits

facts.statement: The fenestrae in the skull of Rukwasuchus are ellipsoidal in shape, unlike the almost circular openings found in Stolokrosuchus.
facts.quote: The fenestrae are described as ellipsoidal in overall shape, which sets them apart from the almost circular openings in the skull of Stolokrosuchus

facts.statement: Unlike in derived neosuchians and modern crocodiles, the optic recess in Rukwasuchus is not closed posteriorly but opens ventrally.
facts.quote: Unlike in derived neosuchians including today's crocodiles the recess is not closed posteriorly but instead opens ventrally

facts.statement: Rukwasuchus is a monotypic genus containing only the single species Rukwasuchus yajabalijekundu.
facts.quote: The genus is monotypic, it contains only a single species, Rukwasuchus yajabalijekundu

facts.statement: In Rukwasuchus, the supraoccipital bone forms a pronounced U-shape due to a ventral deflection caused by the overlying parietal bone.
facts.quote: The supraoccipital is exclusively visible in posterior view as it is fully overlain by the parietal on the skull table, which furthermore forms a ventral deflection that gives this bone a pronounced U-shape.

facts.statement: The otoccipitals dominate the occipital surface of Rukwasuchus, forming a broad U-shaped suture with the supraoccipital between the posttemporal fenestrae.
facts.quote: The otoccipitals dominate the occipital surface and the contact between them and the supraoccipital reflects the contact of the latter with the parietal, forming a broad U-shaped suture stretching between the posttemporal fenestrae.

facts.statement: The laterosphenoid in Rukwasuchus forms the anterolateral wall of the braincase and consists of two laminae separated by a crest.
facts.quote: The laterosphenoid, which forms the anterolateral wall for the braincase, can be divided into two laminae, one anterolateral and one posterolateral which themselves are separated by a crest.

facts.statement: The parabasisphenoid rostrum (cultriform process) in Rukwasuchus is a subrectangular plate that widens dorsally and contacts the laterosphenoid bridge and anterolateral lamina.
facts.quote: The parabasisphenoid rostrum, also known as the cultriform process, extends as a subrectangular plate parallel to the anterior pterygoid process, widens towards its dorsal edge and contacts both the laterosphenoid bridge as well as a small part of the anterolateral laterosphenoid lamina.

facts.statement: The prominence of crest A and the continuous presence of crest B across the quadrate and pterygoid are features shared with other peirosaurians such as Stolokrosuchus, Hamadasuchus, and Montealtosuchus.
facts.quote: The prominence of crest A and continuous presence of crest B across quadrate and pterygoid has also been noted in other peirosaurians like Stolokrosuchus, Hamadasuchus and Montealtosuchus.

facts.statement: Teeth attributed to Rukwasuchus are described as subconical with weak root-crown construction and moderate side-to-side compression.
facts.quote: The teeth are described as subconical with a weak construction between root and crown and moderate labiolingual (side-to-side) compression.

facts.statement: Teeth attributed to Rukwasuchus have distinct denticles on their cutting edges and enamel with longitudinal crenulations and striations, similar to Hamadasuchus.
facts.quote: The mesial and distal cutting edges or carinae of the teeth bear distinct denticles like those seen in Hamadasuchus and the enamel furthermore possess weak crenulations and striations that run down the surface longitudinally.

facts.statement: Although the holotype of Rukwasuchus lacks teeth, several teeth from the Galula Formation have been tentatively assigned to this taxon.
facts.quote: While the holotype of Rukwasuchus preserves neither teeth nor alveoli, several teeth from the Galula Formation have nonetheless been tentatively referred to this taxon.

facts.statement: CT scans of the braincase reveal large parts of the Rukwasuchus endocast, though some internal structures are obscured by damage or matrix.
facts.quote: Thanks to the preservation of the braincase CT scans reveal large parts of the endocast of Rukwasuchus with only some parts of the internal structure obscured by damage or dense matrix still adhering to the fossil.

facts.statement: The Rukwasuchus endocast has an overall shape resembling modern gharials and freshwater crocodiles, with broad cerebrum hemispheres that taper to form a spade-shaped element.
facts.quote: The overall shape resembles modern gharials and freshwater crocodiles, with the two hemispheres of the cerebrum broad and tapering both towards the back and front, forming an element that is spade-shaped and modestly high.

facts.statement: A prominent indentation just behind the cerebrum is a distinct feature of the Rukwasuchus endocast noted in the 2014 description.
facts.quote: Another distinct feature of the endocast of Rukwasuchus noted in the 2014 description is a prominent indentation just behind the cerebrum while the rest of the dorsal endocast surface is more typical in its morphology.

facts.statement: Rukwasuchus exemplifies the blunt morphotype of the dural peak, which appears elongated and rounded in profile view.
facts.quote: Among the two morphotypes recognized by Jorgo Ristevski for this structure, Rukwasuchus exemplifies the blunt form, characterized by a dural peak that in profile view appears elongated and rounded.

facts.statement: The Rukwasuchus endocast bears pericerebral spines accompanied by lateral ridges, features otherwise known only in Zulmasuchus and Campinasuchus among notosuchians.
facts.quote: The endocast of Rukwasuchus also bears a pair of protrusions referred to as the pericerebral spines, which are accompanied by lateral ridges and otherwise only known in Zulmasuchus and Campinasuchus among notosuchians.

facts.statement: The Rukwasuchus pituitary gland is described as rather small, with the pituitary fossa directed almost ventrally.
facts.quote: The pituitary gland is described as rather small and the pituitary fossa, like in the not especially closely related baurusuchids, is directed almost ventrally.

facts.statement: Nicholl and colleagues describe Rukwasuchus as a medium-to-large-bodied animal.
facts.quote: Nicholl and colleagues describe Rukwasuchus as being a medium-to large-bodied animal.

facts.statement: Studies suggest Rukwasuchus diverged after the Argentinian Kinesuchus and Stolokrosuchus from Niger, but before most South American forms.
facts.quote: In both instances Rukwasuchus diverged after the Argentinian Kinesuchus and Stolokrosuchus from Niger, but before the majority of South American forms.

facts.statement: Recent analyses by Ruiz et al. (2024) and Wilberg et al. (2025) place Rukwasuchus in either the subfamily Pepesuchinae or the family Itasuchidae.
facts.quote: Featured below are the results of Ruiz et al. 2024 as well as Wilberg et al. 2025, the former using the name Pepesuchinae whereas the latter places these animals in the family Itasuchidae.

facts.statement: Rukwasuchus is known exclusively from the Namba Member of the Galula Formation in Tanzania, dating from the Cenomanian to Campanian stages of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Rukwasuchus is exclusively known from the Namba Member, the uppermost stratigraphic level of the Galula Formation in Tanzania, which may be as old as the Cenomanian and as young as the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The Namba Member environment was wetter and sub-humid with paleosols matching an open forest, following a climate shift from the underlying seasonally dry Mtuka Member.
facts.quote: While the underlying Mtuka Member appears to represent a seasonally dry, sub-arid environment, the Namba Member was deposited after a subtle shift in climate that changed environmental conditions to be wetter and sub-humid with paleosol matching an open forest environment.

facts.quote: PBDB name: Rukwasuchus (genus), Sertich and O'Connor 2014

facts.quote: Parent group: Peirosauridae

facts.quote: Type species: Rukwasuchus yajabalijekundu

facts.statement: Rukwasuchus lived between 100.5 and 72.2 million years ago, during the Cenomanian to Campanian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Campanian (100.5 to 72.2 million years ago)
